attachment. In AN 10:29, the Buddha recommends this view as conducive to developing dispassion for becoming. However, in MN 106 he warns that it can lead to the refined equanimity of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, which can become an object of clinging. Only if that subtle clinging is detected can all clinging be abandoned. The Canon’s most extended discussion of this theme of meditation is in SN 22:55. See Appendix Two. For more on this topic, see The Paradox of Becoming, chapter 5.
